links.outcome: Attack success rate of image-embedded prompt injection with versus without defenses (cropping, OCR sanitization, ProvDent)
links.effect: OCR-based sanitization gave the strongest attack reduction (pooled ASR 0.2%); all defenses kept clean-image F1 within 0.6 percentage points of baseline.
links.quote: OCR-based sanitization achieved the strongest attack reduction (pooled ASR: 0.2%), while ProvDent provided a complementary fail-open governance mechanism that escalates suspicious cases for human review.

links.outcome: Vulnerability of VLMs to adversarial image-embedded text injection (paired attack success rate)
links.effect: All four models vulnerable; paired attack success rates up to 62.6% (95% CI 58.5–66.7%) for GPT-4o; model-specific vulnerability profiles with significant attack-by-model interactions.
links.quote: All four models were vulnerable, with paired attack success rates up to 62.6% (95% CI: 58.5–66.7%) for GPT-4o.

unlisted_practices: Provenance-aware defense with bounded clinical abstention (ProvDent) for image-embedded prompt injection
OCR-based text sanitization of medical images before VLM inference

screen.practice: input sanitization and prompt injection defense guardrails
screen.reason: The study empirically tests multiple guardrail/defense strategies (cropping, OCR-based text sanitization, provenance-aware bounded abstention) to protect vision-language models against prompt injection in medical imaging.
